newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products steady to weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products steady to weaker in thin trade.

text.p: NWE oil products were steady to slightly weaker on Tuesday in very light trade with many traders absent from the market ahead of Christmas.
Outright physical gas oil prices were helped higher by firmer benchmark IPE futures. January IPE gas oil was $2.25 higher at $213.75 a tonne at 1110 GMT.
Gas oil premiums were pressured down by the rise. Brokers pegged premiums at Jan IPE flat/+5 cents for second half December and Jan IPE +$1/+$2 for second half January delivery.
Two heating oil barges were reported sold midmorning at $213 and $213.25 a tonne.

High sulphur fuel oil barges were weaker at $212/$213 fob ARA. A prompt barge was sold at $110 early on, but traders said this was done by a Rotterdam refinery which needed to offload some material after a power outage problem last week.
Gasoline was slightly weaker in thin trade. A prompt Eurograde barge was reported done at $219 a tonne fob ARA.
